short: Extra stock held to absorb demand spikes and late deliveries.
seoTitle: Safety Stock — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Safety stock is the buffer held above expected demand to absorb two kinds of surprise: a sales spike, and a supplier arriving late.
definition: Safety stock is the buffer held above expected demand to absorb two kinds of surprise: a sales spike, and a supplier arriving late. It is the price of not running out.
bodyHtml:
Why Safety Stock matters

Safety stock is a deliberate trade between the cost of holding stock and the cost of losing a sale. The right level depends on how variable your demand and lead times actually are, not on how cautious you feel.

Safety Stock formula

Safety stock ≈ (Maximum daily usage × Maximum lead time) − (Average daily usage × Average lead time)

Simple, and enough for most small businesses.

How Safety Stock works in practice

Hold more where the item is critical, cheap to store and long-lived; hold less where it is perishable or expensive. Reviewing which items actually caused stockouts last quarter beats applying a blanket rule.

faq.question: How much safety stock is too much?
faq.answer: When holding cost and spoilage risk outweigh the margin on the sales it protects.

faq.question: Do perishables need safety stock?
faq.answer: Very little. For short shelf-life goods, ordering more often beats holding a buffer.
